title: State of Maharashtra v. Charles Gurmukh Sobhraj (The Bikini Killer)
crime_type: Serial Poisoning / Drugging / International Tourist Fraud
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / High Court of Delhi / Sessions Court Delhi
source: Supreme Court of India Official Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/1770281)
ipc_sections: Section 328 IPC (Administering stupefying drug with intent to commit offence)
Section 468 IPC (Forgery for purpose of cheating)
location: Ashoka Hotel & Hotel Vikram, New Delhi, India
evidence: Recovery of chemical sedatives, Mogadon (Nitrazepam), and Largactil pills in hotel suites occupied by accused
Recovery of forged French, British, and Canadian passports with substituted photographs
Medical toxicology reports establishing acute poisoning of French engineering student tour group at Hotel Vikram
Stolen international traveler cheques and pawn records recovered from bank lockers
Eyewitness identification by survivors and hotel receptionists during judicial identification parade
modus_operandi: Approached Western backpackers and tourists along the Hippie Trail by posing as a gem merchant, cultural guide, or luxury traveler. Gained confidence, offered medicated drinks or dysentery pills laced with debilitating tranquilizers (Nitrazepam/Largactil), robbed travel funds and original passports, and in multiple instances strangled or set fire to incapacitated victims to avoid identification.
personality_disorder: Clinical diagnosis documented across international penal institutions: Severe Narcissistic Personality Disorder with Antisocial features, extraordinary superficial charm, pathological grandiosity, con artistry, and high-functioning manipulation.
common_traits: Targeting foreign backpackers and isolated tourists
Charming chameleon persona and false elite status
Use of pharmaceutical sleeping pills and neuroleptics in drinks
Theft of identity documents, passports, and traveler checks
International cross-border mobility to exploit jurisdictional extradition delays
summary: High-profile international criminal case in which Charles Sobhraj was arrested in New Delhi in July 1976 after drugging an entire tour group of 60 French students. Tried and convicted under Section 328 and 302 IPC, serving over two decades in Tihar Central Jail.
